column3: With respect to the Holiday Inn St. Petersburg West Mortgage Loan (2.2%), in a July 2025 franchisor quality evaluation report the Mortgaged Property received failing scores for Cleanliness (82.83%) and Condition (84.76%). The Mortgaged Property also received a 63.42% score for “Guest Love,” which is considered unsatisfactory. However, the hotel received a 100.00% score in the Brand Safety Standard and Brand Standard Major categories, and a 91.60% score in the Brand Standard Important category. The franchisor’s quality evaluation report states that if the hotel fails the Quality Evaluation (84.99% or lower) for the Brand Standard Major, Brand Standard Important, Brand Safety Standards, Cleanliness or Condition categories or the 6-month rolling Guest Love score is in the Unsatisfactory brand threshold, a fee may be assessed, and a “Quality” visit may be scheduled. The report also requires that the non-compliant items be corrected and updated in a corrective action plan within 7 days. Prior to origination, the borrower presented an informal action plan to the lender and advised the lender such plan would go into effect in August 2025. The borrower has advised the lender that such plan has been implemented, and that it is not aware of when the next quality assurance visit by the franchisor will take place. Pursuant to the related franchise agreement, the borrower as franchisee must “provide efficient, courteous and high-quality service to the public including, without limitation, maintaining minimum product and service quality standards and scores for quality assurance and guest survey programs established and maintained by IHG”. A breach of the franchisee’s obligations may constitute grounds for termination, provided that the franchisor notifies the franchisee at least 30 days in advance of the termination date, the notice reasonably identifies the breach and the breach is not fully remedied within the time period specified in the notice.
